subject: Stormbridge: Where is data processed and which subprocessors handle transfers?
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@stormbridge.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@stormbridge.com, Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@stormbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q: processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border transfers

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Stormbridge liked the performance profile. Before we advance the procurement loop, our security and legal teams need a clearer picture of where customer data is actually processed and which third parties (subprocessors) may see or transit the data. Specific asks: 

- Primary processing region(s) for API calls originating in the EU.
- Any subprocessors involved in tokenization, model hosting, monitoring, logging, or observability (names + country).
- Whether we ever route data outside the EU (including US) for model fallback or capacity overflow.
- Typical retention window for raw request logs and KV cache snapshots, and deletion workflow for customer-triggered requests.

Can you send a short bullet summary and any diagrams or inventory spreadsheets? Also, is there an option to keep all processing strictly inside EU regions for an enterprise Private deployment?

Samira
Samira Khan
Director of Platform Security, Stormbridge
samira.k@stormbridge.com

---
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@stormbridge.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, legal@stormbridge.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border transfers

Samira — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary and I attached a high-level data flow diagram plus our current subprocessor inventory spreadsheet. I’ll follow up with Marissa for runbook-level details.

Bullet-summary (short):
- Primary regions: EU (Frankfurt eu-central-1 and Dublin eu-west-1) serve EU-origin traffic by default.
- Subprocessors (examples):
  - Compute: our hosted model-serving clusters (managed by Redwood) run on GCP in eu-west-1 and AWS eu-central-1.
  - Storage/etagging & backups: S3-equivalent object stores in-region; snapshot copies for disaster recovery are geo-redundant but can be restricted per contract.
  - Monitoring/observability: a third-party metrics aggregator (Databridge Metrics) receives anonymized telemetry; full request-level logs are retained in our encrypted vaults — see inventory for addresses and countries.
  - Public cloud networking & CDN providers: only for ancillary assets; not for request body transit.
- Cross-border routing: For Hosted API, we do not intentionally route EU customer request bodies to the US. However, we have a documented fallback policy: if EU capacity is exhausted or a customer is on a global routing policy, requests may be routed to compatible model endpoints in other regions (US or APAC). For Dedicated or Private deployments, requests remain in-customer-region unless the customer authorizes otherwise.
- Retention & deletion:
  - Request logs: default retention 30 days (configurable to shorter windows for enterprise plans).
  - KV cache snapshots: retained up to 7 days by default; persistent checkpointing is customer-configurable.
  - Deletion workflow: customer can request data deletion via Console or API; we then enqueue a deletion job that removes logs and cache snapshots within the SLA window (typically 72 hours for Hosted customers; 24–48 hours for Reserved/Dedicated with contract). For Private, deletion is customer-controlled.

Attachments: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (attached) and subprocessor-inventory-2027.xlsx (attached).

Next steps: happy to set a short call with Marissa (operations lead) and Karthik (privacy) to go through any legal/technical details the Stormbridge team wants to validate. If you'd prefer, we can supply a tailored subprocessor addendum and an options matrix for EU-only processing.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0186

Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q: processing locations, subprocessors, and cross-border transfers

Hi Samira — adding a few technical specifics so your infra team can validate against requirements.}

Technical notes (details):
- Region enforcement: Our control plane supports region pinning. For Hosted customers we recommend setting a policy to pin all production routes to eu-central-1. We also offer a Private VPC deployment where all compute, storage, and control plane components are deployed into your AWS/GCP tenant in-region.
- Subprocessor list (high-level):
  - Cloud compute: AWS EC2 (eu-central-1), GCP Compute (eu-west-1) — used for model serving and autoscale workers.
  - Object storage: AWS S3 (eu-central-1) / GCS buckets (eu-west-1) — used for logs, artifacts; encryption at rest with customer-managed keys available.
  - Metrics/alerting: Databridge Metrics (EU-hosted instance) — only aggregated telemetry is sent by default; raw request metadata stays in-region unless you enable cross-region analytics.
  - Model weights hosting: when using Redwood-curated model repository, we host optimized model artifacts in-region; cross-region replication is off by default.
- Network/transit: TLS 1.3 for all in-flight; private peering available for Dedicated customers to avoid public internet egress.
- Fallback policy detail: our smart routing will only fail over to another region if: 1) the original region is at capacity, and 2) the customer's routing policy allows cross-region fallback. We can set strict no-fallback enforcement for compliance customers.
- Deletion proof: for enterprise contracts we provide deletion manifests and a cryptographic hash-based audit trail showing object IDs and deletion timestamps.

If Stormbridge needs a SOC2 report, we can provide the latest attestation under an NDA — we'll coordinate that from legal.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple follow-ups before we move to procurement: 

1) Please send the latest subprocessor inventory (country column highlighted) and the SOC2 Type II report under NDA.
2) Can you confirm the default retention is 30 days for request logs on Hosted and that we can set it to 7 days? Any fee to reduce retention?
3) We want a strict no-cross-border-fallback option for our pilot (EU-only). How quickly can you enforce that and is it a configuration toggle or contract term?

If you can send the inventory+SOC2 link, I'll loop in procurement to turn this into a PO. Happy to do a 30-minute call next week if that's easier.

Best,
Samira
